trigger: an AccessReview:Attest holder (or a client retry loop) records decisions on one grant without limit, then any get_campaign(include_history=true) read loads and renders them all
summary: Per-grant decision history is unbounded: rows are never pruned (FK RESTRICT plus triggers, by design), up to 4096 B justification each, and every REST GET, MCP get_access_review and Access page read loads all of it. Also raised independently by cpp-safety; unhappy-path (UP-5), sre and enterprise-readiness repeat it as echoes. I5(b) escalation to HIGH was argued but judged not met: the unbounded cost falls on the read path, not on a serialised security operation, so the derived band is MEDIUM. Owner ruling later: cap plus bounded read.
classification_rationale: the history table was documented as bounded in effect but record_attestation had no per-grant cap and the read had no LIMIT

trigger: a future caller of record_attestation is added without running evaluate_attestation_sod first
summary: No tripwire pins that every record_attestation( caller runs evaluate_attestation_sod earlier in the same handler. Latent only (2 callers, both gated), so defence in depth.
classification_rationale: no lexical test pinned that every record_attestation caller runs the gate; two callers exist today and both are gated

trigger: a store failure on record_attestation returns PQerrorMessage text (trigger messages, CONTEXT lines) to the caller and into the failure audit detail

Reported independently by security-guardian and architect (S3). Information disclosure of schema text is minor (no control fails), so derived LOW.
classification_rationale: the failure path surfaced raw database text and the failure-path audit detail used flatten_audit_text rather than audit_token

trigger: a reader of auth-architecture.md or the routed Periodic Access Reviews row relies on the stated audit and enforcement mechanism
summary: Two docs claims contradict the code (lost-COMMIT audit row; where the user rule is decided; also routed-concerns-access-control.md clause 5). Derived at the reporter's native severity per the truth rule: no harmful guidance, output otherwise correct.
classification_rationale: docs say a lost-COMMIT audit row 'may be missing' while the code writes result=failure beside a committed decision, and say the user rule is 'decided in the write' while it is decided in C++ before any lease

trigger: a caller of the store passes an empty reviewer (both handlers derive it from the session, so no route does)

adjudicated_by: owner ruling 2026-11-04 (questions window), supported by security-guardian, architect, sre, compliance-officer and consistency-auditor (governance agents; independence asserted, not verified)
adjudication_rationale: The wedge is recoverable: close the campaign and open a new one (the remedy is stated in the cap message and the docs). The filler is visible and attributed: every history entry carries its reviewer and the Access page shows the superseded entries. The same AccessReview:Attest holder can already close a campaign, so the cap adds no new reach. The cap was the owner's own ruling ('Cap + bounded read') replacing unbounded growth, so the alternative is the unbounded history the cap closed. The I5(c) raise (a state machine wedged with no recovery) is therefore judged not met. The change's git author is the owner's account, so a literal self-naming check against git authors WILL match and the 'not the change's author' separation is not met in the literal sense; independence here rests on the governance agents named, which are subagents of the authoring session and so not independent in the SKILL.md sense. It is an audit trail of the ruling, not a verified control.
